ble.notes: Name-based discovery is primary (MIBCS / MIBFS / MI_SCALE prefixes): 0x181D appears only on v1, while v2 advertises 0x181B and also broadcasts weight/impedance in advertisement Service Data (AD type 0x16), which can be read passively without connecting. Zepp Life's advertisement parser handles 0x181B and 0xFEE0 Service Data for v2 and 0x181D Service Data as v1 10-byte weight frames, so passive reading covers v1 too.

identification.notes: Service UUID 0x181D is present on v1 only; v2 (MIBCS) exposes 0x181B instead, so filtering on 0x181D misses v2 scales. Discover by advertised name — MIBCS, MIBFS, MI_SCALE — as openScale does.

device.name: Xiaomi Mi Scale Body Composition Scale
device.notes:
Xiaomi Mi Scale v1 and v2 body composition scales. v1 is weight-only; v2 adds impedance measurement for body composition (body fat, muscle, water, bone mass, visceral fat, BMR). Price $20-30. Body composition is computed client-side from the impedance reading; the metric math originates from Holtek (the scale's MCU OEM) — Zepp Life ships it as a JNI wrapper (a Holtek body-fat class loading a native body-fat library) — and openScale's MiScaleLib is the reverse-engineered port. A newer Xiaomi Body Composition Scale S400 (MJTZC01YM) exists and is handled by openScale's separate MiScaleS400Handler.
PROTOCOL: uses BLE standard Weight Scale service (0x181D) plus a custom Mi vendor service (0x1530) for v2 configuration. Weight readings arrive as live 13-byte (v2) or 10-byte (v1) notifications. History data is downloaded via a handshake protocol on characteristic 0x2A2F.
WEIGHT FRAME (10-byte, both variants): [ctrl_byte] [weight_lo] [weight_hi] [year_lo] [year_hi] [month] [day] [hour] [min] [sec]. Control byte bits: Bit0=LBS, Bit4=Jin, Bit5=Stabilized, Bit7=WeightRemoved. Valid only when Bit5=1 AND Bit7=0. Weight division: /100 for lbs/jin, /200 for kg. Weight value 0xFFF0 (65520) is a sentinel (overload / no valid reading), not a measurement — Zepp Life's parsers special-case it.
v2 LIVE FRAME (13-byte): [ctrl0] [ctrl1] [year_lo] [year_hi] [month] [day] [hour] [min] [sec] [imp_lo] [imp_hi] [weight_lo] [weight_hi]. This does NOT extend the 10-byte layout — two control bytes come first and weight sits at bytes 11-12, not bytes 1-2. Control byte 0: Bit0=LBS. Control byte 1: Bit1=hasImpedance, Bit5=Stabilized, Bit6=isCatty, Bit7=WeightRemoved. Impedance at bytes 9-10 (uint16 LE) when hasImpedance=1. Zepp Life's v2 frame parser matches this layout exactly, including /100 scaling for lbs and jin vs /200 for kg, and treats weight 0xFFF0 as an overload sentinel (forced unstabilized).
HISTORY DOWNLOAD: enable notify on 0x2A2F, then write `01 <ts:uint32le>` = "count records since unix timestamp ts" — the `01 96 8A BD 62` in older docs is NOT fixed magic, it is this opcode with one hardcoded ts (0x62BD8A96). The scale replies `01 <count:uint16le>`. Write `02` to trigger the transfer; records arrive as concatenated 10-byte (v1) / 13-byte (v2) frames in the live-frame layout until a notification of 1 byte or less ends the stream. Finish with `03` (also aborts); if exactly `count` records arrived, confirm the sync point with `04 <ts:uint32le>`. Decoded from Zepp Life's sync profile; app-derived, not hardware-verified.
UNIT CONFIG: set scale unit via vendor characteristic 0x1542 under service 0x1530 with `06 04 00 <unit>` (0=kg/SI, 1=lbs/imperial, 2=jin/catty — matches Zepp Life's weight-unit enum KG=0/POUND=1/ JIN=2). The app writes further 0x1542 commands: opcode `06` with sub-commands 05, 0A, 0B, 0F, 10, 11, 12 (mode/user management) and, on v2, opcode `04` with args 01-04; their semantics are only partially understood (medium confidence). Documented on v2; the openScale wiki's v1 GATT dump also lists 0x1530 with 0x1531/0x1532/0x1542/0x1543, so the vendor service is NOT v2-only.
DISCOVERY: advertised names: "MIBCS", "MIBFS", "MI SCALE2", "MI_SCALE_*". Service UUID 0x181D is present on v1 only — v2 (MIBCS) exposes 0x181B with 0x2A9C Body Composition Measurement (indicate), not 0x181D/0x2A9D, so a 0x181D scan filter misses v2. openScale discovers by advertised name, which is the robust path. Zepp Life matches names by regex (a MI/MIBCS/MIBFS brand rule), so exact advertised strings like "MI SCALE2" are NOT confirmed by the app and remain community-sourced. v2 broadcasts weight/impedance in its advertisements (Service Data, AD type 0x16), enabling passive connectionless reading; Zepp Life's advertisement parser also handles 0x181D Service Data as v1 10-byte weight frames (plus a 0xFEE0 service-data variant), so passive reading covers v1 as well.
CONFIDENCE: HIGH for all UUIDs, weight frame format, control bits, history protocol, and v2 impedance frames — sourced from github.com/oliexdev/openScale, a production Android app with years of real-world use across hundreds of users. The v2 13-byte frame layout, unit enum, and service/characteristic bindings (0x181D + 0x2A9D/0x2A2B/0x2A2F on v1; 0x181B + 0x2A9C on v2; vendor 0x1530 with 0x1542/0x1543 and DFU 0x1531/0x1532) are independently corroborated by the Zepp Life app (jadx, 2026). Details decoded only from the app and not verified on hardware (history-sync parameterization, extra 0x1542 sub-commands, 0xFFF0 sentinel, advertisement Service Data parsing) are MEDIUM confidence.

credentials.notes: BLE-only. No auth. Health data — handle with privacy awareness.

factory_reset.effect: Remove battery to clear internal state. No credential storage.

steps.action: Remove batteries for 30 seconds and reinsert.

methods.description: Scan for 0x181D service, connect, subscribe for weight notifications. No pairing required for basic reading.

steps.action: Step on scale to wake it.
Scan for 0x181D Weight Scale service or known name prefixes (MIBCS, MIBFS, MI_SCALE) and connect.
Subscribe to notifications on 0x2A9D (weight measurement) and/or 0x2A2F (history).

setup.notes: No provisioning. Scale advertises when stepped on or powered. For history download, sync current time to 0x2A2B before requesting data.

rejoin.notes: No bonding. Scale accepts connections from any central.

variants.notes: Weight only, no impedance. Service 0x181D. 10-byte frames. History on 0x2A2F under 0x181D. The openScale wiki's v1 GATT dump also lists vendor service 0x1530 (0x1531/0x1532/0x1542/0x1543), so the vendor service is not v2-only.
Body composition via impedance. Service 0x181B (primary) + 0x1530 vendor service. 13-byte live frames with impedance. Unit config via 0x1542.
Same as v2, different advertised name prefix.

v2 capabilities. The exact advertised name "MI SCALE2" is community-sourced only: Zepp Life matches device names by regex (a MI/MIBCS/MIBFS brand rule), so the app cannot confirm the literal string. Treat the exact name as unverified.

entities.name: Weight
entities.notes: v1 only — the body-composition models carry weight in the 0x2A9C frame instead (see the second Weight entity). kg is the out-of-box unit. When the scale is switched to pounds or jin, the bound field's unit_values and unit_scales give the unit and scaling in force.

entities.name: Weight
entities.notes: From the 13-byte v2 frame. kg is the out-of-box unit; the bound field's unit_values and unit_scales follow this frame's unit_flags.

entities.name: Impedance
entities.notes: Rebound from the 0x2A2F history stream (a concatenation of records with no fixed offset) to the live 0x2A9C frame, which is where a body-composition scale reports impedance as it measures. Valid only while control_1 bit 1 is set. v1 scales have no impedance.

entities.name: Unit
entities.notes: No select_option command is bound because no set command is declared — the unit-set frame (06 04 00 <unit>) is documented only in the 0x1542 characteristic notes, so a binding-only consumer renders this entity hidden until that frame is promoted to a command.

dfu_mode.notes: How the scale appears while updating is not established.

enter.notes: The DFU control point 0x1531 and packet 0x1532 sit in the Mi vendor service 0x1530 in normal mode, beside the 0x1542 unit configuration. How the app starts an update on them is not established.

image.notes: OTAs are delivered device-bound through the Zepp Life app; there are no public firmware files.

dfu.notes: App-derived (Zepp Life's DFU profile binds service 0x1530 with control point 0x1531 and packet 0x1532), not hardware-verified. The layout mirrors Nordic's legacy DFU (1530/1531/1532) but on the Huami 0000xxxx-0000-3512-2118-0009af100700 base, not Nordic's …-1212-efde-1523-785feabcd123, so a Nordic legacy client will not find it, and whether the opcodes match Nordic's is not established (hence `huami_dfu`, not nordic_legacy_dfu). dfu.services is omitted because 0x1530 also carries the unit configuration a client does need to write.

remaining_unknowns:
The weight fields' unit is a bit field of the same frame (pounds, jin or kilograms, each with its own divisor), which `unit_values` — a raw-value-to-unit table — cannot express; the format blocks declare the kilogram decode and describe the other two in notes, so a consumer must test the control bits itself.
0x2A2F history notifications concatenate whole records and interleave the count reply and the end marker, so they carry no format block; a client walks them in record-sized steps using the 0x2A9D (v1) or 0x2A9C (v2) layout.
Neither frame layout has been read back from a scale by this project; both rest on openScale and Zepp Life's parsers.

format.name: control
format.notes: Bit field, not a code: bit 0 = pounds, bit 4 = jin (catty), bit 5 = stabilised, bit 7 = weight removed. The two unit bits are also declared on their own as unit_flags below.

format.name: unit_flags
format.notes: Bits 0 and 4 of the control byte: the unit weight_raw is in.

format.name: weight_raw
format.notes: The scale reports in whichever unit it is set to, and changing the unit changes the resolution too: kilograms at raw / 200, pounds and jin at raw / 100. unit_values and unit_scales state both from unit_flags. The 0x1542 unit command selects which unit the scale uses.

characteristics.name: Weight Measurement
characteristics.notes: Standard BLE Weight Measurement characteristic. Often absent on Mi scales — weight arrives via 0x2A2F instead. When present, carries 10-byte weight frame. The frame is the v1 layout in device.notes, NOT the SIG Weight Measurement layout (whose flags byte would put a 0.005 kg / 0.01 lb weight at the same offsets but with different scaling and no timestamp). Layout from openScale's Mi Scale handler and Zepp Life's frame parser; reported, not read back by this project. Weight is only valid when control bit 5 (stabilised) is set and bit 7 (weight removed) is clear; raw 0xFFF0 is an overload sentinel.

characteristics.name: History
characteristics.notes: Custom history characteristic. Per Zepp Life's sync profile: write `01 <ts:uint32le>` ("count records since unix time ts" — the previously documented fixed magic `01 96 8A BD 62` is this opcode with ts=0x62BD8A96, not a constant); the scale replies `01 <count:uint16le>`. Write `02` to trigger the transfer and collect concatenated 10-byte (v1) / 13-byte (v2) records until a notification of 1 byte or less ends the stream. Finish with `03`; on a complete transfer confirm with `04 <ts:uint32le>`. App-derived, not hardware-verified (medium confidence). No format block: the notifications are a concatenation of whole records (a v1 unit can pack two 10-byte records into one 20-byte notification) interleaved with the 1-byte end marker and the `01 <count>` reply, so no fixed offset holds across the stream. Each record has the 0x2A9D layout on v1 and the 0x2A9C layout on v2; a client walks the buffer in record-sized steps.

characteristics.name: Current Time
characteristics.notes: Write current time before history download: `[year_lo, year_hi, month, day, hour, min, sec, 0x00, 0x00, 0x01]`

services.name: Weight Scale Service
services.notes: Standard BLE Weight Scale service. Present on v1; the independent v2 (MIBCS) GATT dump shows NO 0x181D — v2 exposes 0x181B with 0x2A9C instead. Carries weight measurement (0x2A9D), weight scale feature (0x2A9E), current time (0x2A2B), and Mi history (0x2A2F).

characteristics.name: Mi Config
characteristics.notes: Set scale unit: `06 04 00 <unit>` where 0=kg/SI, 1=lbs/imperial, 2=jin/catty (matches Zepp Life's weight-unit enum KG=0/POUND=1/JIN=2). Zepp Life also writes opcode `06` with sub-commands 05, 0A, 0B, 0F, 10, 11, 12 and, on v2, opcode `04` with args 01-04 (mode/user management; semantics only partially understood — medium confidence).

characteristics.name: DFU Control Point
characteristics.notes: BLE DFU control point for firmware updates, together with the 0x1532 DFU Packet characteristic.

characteristics.name: DFU Packet
characteristics.notes: DFU data channel; firmware image is streamed here.

characteristics.name: Low Battery
characteristics.notes: Low-battery indication (uint8; always 0x01 in the ble-in-xiaomi v2 GATT dump).

services.name: Mi Vendor Service
services.notes: Present on v2 and — per the openScale wiki's v1 GATT dump — on v1 as well, so it is not v2-only. Provides unit configuration via 0x1542, a BLE DFU firmware-update channel via 0x1531/0x1532 (OTAs are delivered device-bound via the Zepp Life app; no public firmware files), and a low-battery characteristic 0x1543. Zepp Life binds exactly this layout: its weight profiles attach 0x1542/0x1543 under 0x1530, and its DFU profile uses service 0x1530 with control point 0x1531 and packet 0x1532.

format.name: control_1
format.notes: Bit 1 = impedance present, bit 5 = stabilised, bit 6 = jin (catty), bit 7 = weight removed.

format.name: unit_flags
format.notes: The two unit bits, read as one little-endian word over both control bytes: bit 0 is control_0 bit 0 (pounds) and bit 14 is control_1 bit 6 (jin).

format.name: impedance
format.notes: Body impedance in ohms, the input to the client-side body composition maths. Only meaningful when control_1 bit 1 is set; otherwise the scale has not finished measuring.

format.name: weight_raw
format.notes: Kilograms at raw / 200 when neither unit bit is set; pounds at raw / 100 when control_0 bit 0 is set; jin at raw / 100 when control_1 bit 6 is set. unit_values and unit_scales state both from unit_flags.

characteristics.name: Body Composition Measurement
characteristics.notes: Standard Body Composition Measurement — the v2 GATT dump shows 0x2A9C with indicate, not the 0x2A9D Weight Measurement. What it carries is the 13-byte v2 live frame from device.notes, not the SIG Body Composition layout: two control bytes, a timestamp, impedance and then weight. Layout from openScale's v2 handler and Zepp Life's parser (reported, not read back here). Weight is valid when control byte 1 bit 5 (stabilised) is set and bit 7 (weight removed) is clear; impedance is meaningful only when control byte 1 bit 1 is set; raw weight 0xFFF0 is an overload sentinel.

services.name: Body Composition Service (v2 only)
services.notes: v2 primary service. Carries history, current time, and the body composition measurement for v2 scales.
